# Allocator

The operations every allocator provides.

```rux
pub interface Allocator {
    func Allocate(
        &var self,
        layout: Layout
    ) -> *var opaque throws AllocError;
    func Deallocate(
        &var self,
        block: *var opaque,
        layout: Layout
    ) throws AllocError;
    func Reallocate(
        &var self,
        block: *var opaque,
        oldLayout: Layout,
        newLayout: Layout
    ) -> *var opaque throws AllocError;
}
```

Written as an interface so a generic can require it — `func Build<A: Allocator>(allocator: &var A)` borrows the
caller's allocator and resolves calls at each instantiation with nothing dispatched at run time — and so a call
can borrow any allocator as `&var Allocator`.
Every operation may write its receiver: an arena advances its pointer and a pool its free lists.
A container keeps its allocator as an `Allocator` value, which is a copyable handle to the implementation and owns
nothing. A stateless allocator such as [`SystemAllocator`](/docs/api/allocator/system-allocator) converts to one anywhere and stays valid forever; a
stateful one gives a handle only through an `unsafe` `Handle`, whose caller promises the allocator outlives it.

## Requirements

<h3 id="allocate"><code>Allocate</code></h3>

```rux
func Allocate(
    &var self,
    layout: Layout
) -> *var opaque throws AllocError
```

Takes storage matching `layout` and reports where it landed.
The address satisfies the layout's alignment. The contents are undefined.
A zero-sized layout gives a non-null aligned address that nothing may be read from or written to.
The storage is the caller's until [`Deallocate`](/docs/api/allocator/allocator#deallocate) takes it back with an equal layout.

| Name     | Type     | Description                   |
| -------- | -------- | ----------------------------- |
| `layout` | `Layout` | the size and alignment wanted |

**Returns**: the address of the storage, or why none was taken

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/Contract.rux#L40)

<h3 id="deallocate"><code>Deallocate</code></h3>

```rux
func Deallocate(
    &var self,
    block: *var opaque,
    layout: Layout
) throws AllocError
```

Gives back storage that this allocator handed out.
`block` must be an address this allocator returned, and `layout` must equal the layout it was given with.
Reports `InvalidBlock` where the allocator can tell, and is undefined where it cannot.
Every pointer into the block becomes invalid, and the storage may be handed to the next allocation at once.

| Name     | Type          | Description                        |
| -------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `block`  | `*var opaque` | an address this allocator returned |
| `layout` | `Layout`      | the layout it was allocated with   |

**Returns**: nothing when the release was accepted, or why it was refused

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/Contract.rux#L50)

<h3 id="reallocate"><code>Reallocate</code></h3>

```rux
func Reallocate(
    &var self,
    block: *var opaque,
    oldLayout: Layout,
    newLayout: Layout
) -> *var opaque throws AllocError
```

Changes the size of a block, preserving as much of its contents as both layouts hold.
`block` and `oldLayout` describe the existing allocation; `newLayout` is what is wanted. The address reported
may or may not be the address it was given, so the caller must use what comes back.
On success the first `min(old, new)` bytes are preserved and the original block is gone. On failure the
original block is untouched and still the caller's.
A `newLayout` of size zero reports the shared empty address, exactly as [`Allocate`](/docs/api/allocator/allocator#allocate) would, so the result is
always releasable with the layout it was asked for.
The two layouts must have the same alignment. An allocator reports `Unsupported` rather than silently moving
a block to a different alignment.
The old pointer is invalid once this succeeds, whether or not the address changed.

| Name        | Type          | Description                                           |
| ----------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `block`     | `*var opaque` | the existing allocation's address                     |
| `oldLayout` | `Layout`      | the layout `block` was allocated with                 |
| `newLayout` | `Layout`      | the layout wanted, which must have the same alignment |

**Returns**: the address the block is at afterwards, or why it was not resized

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/Contract.rux#L67)

## Implementations

| Type                                                      | Summary                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`Arena`](/docs/api/allocator/arena)                      | An allocator that advances a pointer and reclaims everything at once. |
| [`FixedBuffer`](/docs/api/allocator/fixed-buffer)         | An allocator that advances a pointer through storage it does not own. |
| [`Pool`](/docs/api/allocator/pool)                        | An allocator that serves small blocks from per-class free lists.      |
| [`SystemAllocator`](/docs/api/allocator/system-allocator) | An allocator that asks the operating system for pages.                |

## Related

<h3 id="empty-block"><code>EmptyBlock</code></h3>

```rux
pub const EmptyBlock: uint = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF0000;
```

The address a zero-sized allocation reports.
Not null, so a caller need not branch, and aligned to anything, so it satisfies every layout. Nothing may be read
from or written to it: it is an address that exists rather than storage that does.
Every allocator in this package returns exactly this for a zero-sized layout, which makes a zero-sized block
recognizable and its release free.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/Contract.rux#L77)

<h3 id="empty-block-address"><code>EmptyBlockAddress</code></h3>

```rux
pub func EmptyBlockAddress() -> *var opaque
```

The address a zero-sized allocation reports, as a pointer.
Takes nothing and returns the same value every time.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/Contract.rux#L84)

**Returns**: the address every zero-sized allocation reports

<h3 id="is-empty-block"><code>IsEmptyBlock</code></h3>

```rux
pub func IsEmptyBlock(block: *var opaque) -> bool
```

Whether `block` is the address a zero-sized allocation reports.
`block` is read by value and never dereferenced.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Allocator/Src/Contract.rux#L94)

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type          | Description                             |
| ------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `block` | `*var opaque` | the address to test, never dereferenced |

**Returns**: whether it is the address a zero-sized allocation reports
